Add .ai file to gitignore

Add unit tests for `binCollectionDatesService` and configure Jest
- Created `binCollectionDatesService.test.js` to cover utility methods: `parseDotNetDate`, `extractModelDataFromHtml`, `parseMonthCollectionDates`, and `dedupeByUprnTypeDate`. - Updated `binCollectionDatesService` exports to include tested methods. - Added `jest` as a dev dependency and updated `package-lock.json`.

Add UPRN indexes and refactor Contacts to one-to-many
- Add `unique: true` to Address.uprn and `index: true` to BinCollectionDates.uprn to index the foreign key used in queries across all collections - Refactor Contacts from one-record-per-address to one-to-many: scalar `uprn` becomes a `uprns` array; `email` gains `unique: true` as the deduplication key - createContact now upserts by email and pushes the UPRN into the array, allowing one contact to be linked to multiple addresses - Address deletion pulls the UPRN from affected contacts and removes any contacts whose `uprns` array becomes empty
Updated README.md to reflect recent changes
Standardized error logging to use debug module instead of consolse.logs
Removed unused sass compilation
Removed home.ejs as it was unused and updated routes to redirect to addresses

Extracted inline <script> blocks from addresses/new.ejs and bin-collections/show.ejs into public/javascripts/address-picker.js and calendar.js respectively. The single EJS data-injection line in bin-collections/show.ejs remains inline so the server-side collection data is available as a global before calendar.js runs.

king tree has uncommitted edits to views/addresses/index.ejs (improved cing copy/UX on the /addresses page: clearer intro paragraph, an tate message when no addresses are saved, and a govuk-hint explaining e Continue/Manage Address buttons do) and views/addresses/show.ejs d a stale <!-- TODO: Create a delete route for addresses--> comment, hat route already exists).
Made UI/UX improvments to the calendar screen
Added support for bin collection type cgw and updated CSS and JavaScript for garden waste collection.

Accessibility - prevMonth/todayButton/nextMonth are now real <button type="button"> elements (with matching CSS reset) instead of <a href="#">. - #calendar-grid has role="grid", weeks are wrapped in role="row" (via a display: contents wrapper so the CSS grid layout is unaffected), and each day cell has role="gridcell" plus a per-cell aria-label (e.g. "Friday 20 June, Household waste collection"). Padding cells from adjacent months are aria-hidden. - The month/year heading has aria-live="polite" so screen readers announce month changes on navigation.
Mobile agenda view - Below the GOV.UK tablet breakpoint (640px), the grid/weekday header are hidden and replaced by a simple agenda list (#calendar-agenda) of just the days that have a collection that month, colour-coded by type, with an empty state ("No collections this month."). At tablet width and up, it's the reverse — agenda hidden, grid shown.
URL persistence - Prev/Next/Today now push ?year=&month= into the URL via history.pushState. A popstate listener restores the right month on browser back/forward, and reading those params on page load means a refresh (or a shared link) lands on the same month.
Verified all of this with a jsdom-based smoke test (temporarily installed, not added to package.json, removed afterward) — confirmed grid/row/gridcell roles, aria-labels, agenda population, URL updates on navigation, back-button restoration, and deep-linking via query params all work. Couldn't do a real-browser/Docker run (still no docker group access on this machine), so this is DOM-logic-level verification rather than a full visual check — worth a quick look once you're able to load the page in an actual browser, especially the breakpoint switch and button styling.
